logp.method_description: The LogP value for 1–3 was determined using the shake-flask method and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The 1-octanol used in this experiment was pre-saturated with water. A DMSO solution of 1–3 (10 μL, 10 mM) was incubated with 1-octanol (495 μL) and H2O (495 μL) in a 1.5 mL tube. The tube was shaken at room temperature for 24 h. The two phases were separated by centrifugation and the content of 1–3 in the water phase was determined by ICP-MS.

The experiment involves dissolving a test compound (Co1 and Co2) in pre-saturated n-octanol and mixing it with pre-saturated water (1:1 ratio) in a sealed vial. The mixture is shaken (25 °C, 24 h) to reach partitioning equilibrium, followed by phase separation via centrifugation or careful pipetting. Compound concentrations in both phases are quantified using ICP-MS, and logP is calculated as the logarithm of the octanol-to-water concentration ratio (LogP = log(Coctanol/Cwater)). This method adheres to OECD guidelines and is suitable for compounds with logP values between -2 and 4.
